mechanisms.name: Fiscal funding gap
mechanisms.description: Available resources meet some planned expenditure. The remaining recurring funding need is generated by accounting. This is not a prediction of specific service cuts.
mechanisms.equation:
R = compulsory revenue + other revenue
F = max(E - R, 0) * (1 - transition)
Gap = max(E - R - F, 0)
Funded spending = min(E, R + F)
research_gaps: Debt-principal repayments require maturity schedules. Unknown repayments remain null.
Surpluses are not accumulated into a reserve stock in this first recurring-flow calculation.

mechanisms.name: Compulsory revenue cap
mechanisms.description: The starting compulsory-revenue share of GDP is the imposed cap. Collection effectiveness can fall during the transition. Historical receipt shares do not establish a Laffer maximum.
mechanisms.equation:
C = cap * GDP / 100 * collection
collection = 1 - transition * (1 - target effectiveness)
research_gaps: Estimate collectible revenue under mobility, avoidance, enforcement, and changes in the tax base.
Review mandatory and voluntary social contributions separately.

mechanisms.name: Real output
mechanisms.description: Real GDP growth is an exploratory input. Productive capacity stays at 100. Asset repricing does not change either variable by itself.
research_gaps: Quantify output dependence on financing, maintenance, institutional support, and coordination.

mechanisms.name: Planned expenditure
mechanisms.description: Historical expenditure sets the starting scale. A visible real spending-growth input defines commitments. Allocation among services and debt interest is unresolved.
mechanisms.equation: E = baseline expenditure * (1 + real spending growth)^(month / 12)
research_gaps: Model civilian and coercive spending priorities separately.

mechanisms.name: Other recurring revenue
mechanisms.description: Revenue outside the compulsory-revenue proxy includes grants, resource income, and other receipts. Its survival is an exploratory assumption.
mechanisms.equation: Other revenue = baseline other revenue * (1 + growth)^(month / 12)
research_gaps: Separate recurring revenue from asset sales, compulsory fees, and grants dependent on other governments.

mechanisms.name: Transition timing
mechanisms.description: Onset and duration impose the fraction of the transition completed. The same timing withdraws financing coverage and applies the asset-price decline. This timing does not derive one condition from another.
research_gaps: Establish transition timing and whether financing withdrawal and asset repricing occur together. The initial shared timing is imposed.

mechanisms.name: Financing withdrawal
mechanisms.description: Financing covers the recurring deficit before transition. Its coverage fraction is imposed by transition timing. The amount covered is calculated from spending and revenue. Private financing remains outside this government channel.
research_gaps: Determine how borrowing and monetary financing fail, and distinguish them. The initial combined channel does not estimate their separate shares.

mechanisms.name: Real asset repricing
mechanisms.description: Stocks and gross property prices start at 100 and lose at least 80% of their purchasing-power value. Both follow the imposed transition path. These are price indices, not total returns or owners' equity.
research_gaps: Estimate separate asset paths and debt effects. The common path is imposed.

mechanisms.name: Shared purchasing-power index
mechanisms.description: One fixed measurement basis applies to every country. The simulated index compounds the inflation input. It does not measure national living-cost differences or reproduce ShadowStats.
mechanisms.equation:
P = 100 * (1 + annual inflation)^(month / 12)
Dollar asset index = real index * P / 100
research_gaps: Specify a defensible historical inflation series and projection method before treating this path as a forecast.

mechanisms.name: Bitcoin purchasing power
mechanisms.description: Bitcoin real growth is a comparison assumption. Its dollar index combines that path with the shared inflation index. Absolute Bitcoin prices are not inferred.
mechanisms.equation:
Bitcoin real index = 100 * (1 + real growth)^(month / 12)
Bitcoin dollar index = Bitcoin real index * P / 100
Asset Bitcoin index = asset real index * 100 / Bitcoin real index
research_gaps: Choose and evaluate mechanisms for adoption, bubbles, drawdowns, and volatility.

mechanisms.name: Public services
mechanisms.description: A recurring funding gap creates allocation pressure. It does not determine which services survive.
research_gaps: Source spending by function and the resources needed for each service.

mechanisms.name: Capital controls and conflict
mechanisms.description: Fiscal pressure may affect coercive policy. No event likelihood is calculated.
research_gaps: Research jurisdiction-specific controls, redistribution, and war mechanisms.

mechanisms.name: Private institutions
mechanisms.description: Private finance and voluntary organization can sustain production and replace services.
research_gaps: Investigate working capital, private credit, ownership transfers, and viable organizational scale.

mechanisms.name: AI and technology
mechanisms.description: Technology can change productivity and depend on institutional financing.
research_gaps: Calibrate AI, robotics, energy, and space dependencies without counting effects twice.

mechanisms.name: Family life
mechanisms.description: Unmet care and income needs can change household arrangements.
research_gaps: Compare family transfers, employers, paid services, and mutual aid.

mechanisms.name: Demographics
mechanisms.description: Fertility, mortality, migration, and community retention determine population composition.
research_gaps: Source age structure, causal delays, and community transmission.

limitations: These are uncalibrated conditional calculations. No real-world probabilities are assigned.
Historical fiscal shares are applied at the forecast origin without a 2024-to-2026 nowcast. Different source years limit country comparisons.
The revenue cap is stipulated. It is not an estimated Laffer maximum.
Unknown debt maturities, reserves, temporary asset sales, and arrears are excluded from the recurring-flow chart and explicitly unmodeled.
Country government coverage differs. Central-government views exclude subnational institutions.
No automatic link connects asset-price collapse to output, tax receipts, or institutional failure.
Inflation and Bitcoin paths are imposed. Currency displays are indexed comparisons, not absolute exchange rates.
